content_html:
The essence of architectural work - Part 5

In the previous post, we concluded the discussion of the Why, the purpose of architectural work, by looking at the cognitive and the humane facets of architectural work. We also briefly discussed that AI agents are not able to satisfy these traits of architectural work unless you solve solved problems time and again.

In this post, we will move on to the next dimension of architectural work, the What, and discuss the different activities that make up architectural work.

The laws of architectural work

Before we discuss the activities that make up architectural work, let us first briefly revisit the two “laws of architerctural work”. As stated in the referenced blog post, they are not so much actual laws but rather “hard-won findings”. The first law is:

Every decision has its price. No decision is for free.

This means that there is no free lunch in architectural work. Every decision has some up- and some downsides. There is no “right” or “wrong” in architectural work. There are only more or less suitable decisions 1. Thus, no matter what some people try to make you believe (usually to buy their products or services), rest assured that their “perfect” architectures are not perfect. They just decided to hide the downsides of the decisions they made.

Asking how to determine the up- and downsides brings us to the second law:

A decision can only be evaluated with respect to its context.

The ups and downs of architectural decisions are determined by the context in which they are made. While a decision may be perfectly fine in one place, it may be nonsense in another. In short: context matters – as so often.

The 4E framework

With these two “laws”, let us move on to the activities that define architectural work. I developed a small framework to organize them. Rest assured: I will not unpack a TOGAF-weight framework. While such frameworks may also have their value in certain contexts, I am not a big fan of them. I prefer minimal frameworks instead of maximal frameworks. Frameworks that support you in organizing and directing thoughts and work instead of trying to capture every possible detail and forcing you to “tailor” them to your context.

The 4E framework is no difference. I designed it with Simon Brown’s C4 model in mind: something simple, yet useful, that you can memorize without effort. In its core, it is 4 words 2. As with the C4 model, you may argue that it misses a detail here or there, and it is true. The intention of the 4E framework is not to capture every possible detail. Its intention is to capture the essence of architectural work, and I think it does the job well.

Let me explain the 4 parts of the framework in anecdotal form (as it simplifies the memorization even further).

I discussed architectural work with many people, often, but not always, being developers. When I asked them what the core activities of architectural work are, quick as a shot they came up with Explore.

Explore - Find solution options

Explore is about designing solution options: designing structures and behavior, combining frameworks, tools, technologies, and more – everything needed to design an architecture. Note that most people talked about designing the solution, i.e., they used the singular form and not the plural form as I did. I will explain in the next post (link will follow) why this distinction is important.

The design of an architecture is an essential activity. It also cannot be omitted, as every solution has an architecture, i.e., we always design an architecture. We can only decide if we design the architecture explicitly or implicitly, i.e., accidentally as a byproduct of writing code. While I know there were some proponents of implicit design of an architecture at the peak of the Agile hype, calling it “emergent architecture”, I strongly recommend the explicit variant. 3

Oftentimes, architectural work is reduced to the Explore activities. The problem with only designing a solution is that you don’t know if and how the solution delivers to the Why of architecture, as we discussed it in the previous posts. Maybe it creates a working solution. At least we hope so. But does it minimize the cumulative costs of a system over its lifetime without compromising the correctness of behavior at runtime? Does it condense and structure the problem domain and provide guidance and orientation in the solution domain? Does it improve the lives of the people affected?

Maybe. Maybe not. We do not know. We only designed this solution based on our beliefs in a vacuum (which is another reason why architecture often is a subject of heated, yet groundless discussions).

Therefore, I told my peers that Explore is good and needed, yet not sufficient. I asked them for more. Usually, this made them think for a moment. Then someone mentioned that architects tend to communicate a lot, and thus, this has to be another activity. I.e., they touched Execute.

Execute - Help stakeholders make the best possible decisions

Execute is what I call helping the stakeholders involved make the best possible decisions in their contexts. I do not talk about making decisions as an architect but about supporting other people in making decisions because most of the time, we as architects do not make the decisions. The decisions are made by other stakeholders. Even if we think we make the decisions, more often than not it is an illusion.

E.g., many architects think they decide what architecture gets implemented. But in reality, the developers decide which architecture they implement. If they are convinced that the architecture we designed is good, they will implement it. Otherwise, they will use their significant brainpower to avoid implementing it. Even if we try to force them into implementing “our” architecture by adding reviews and other controls to the process, they will find ways around it. Additionally, it is a futile battle. Energy is wasted that could be used in much better ways.

Therefore, I prefer to say that as architects, we support other stakeholders in making good decisions. This requires a lot of communication, collaboration, convincing, and so on. The point is that people usually do not make bad decisions because they are ignorant or malevolent. More often than not, they make bad decisions because they lack relevant information. As an architect, we talk to multiple stakeholder groups, which often gives us information that other stakeholder groups are missing. Organizing this information and sharing it, thereby supporting the different stakeholder groups to base their decisions on a more comprehensive basis, leads to better decisions overall.

Therefore, this is another essential activity.

Neglecting relevant stakeholder groups

A typical project has a dozen or more stakeholder groups. Each of them has very different needs, a very different view on the project, speaks a different language, and so on. Therefore, it is important to learn to understand them as an architect if you really want to support them in making the best decisions possible in their contexts.

This is a place where I often experience shortcomings. Most people who call themselves architects fall into one of two categories:

  • “Developer architects”
  • “Non-developer architects”

The first ones are typically senior developers who started to take on more responsibility and thus started to call themselves “architects”, often reinforced by enterprise career paths that put “architect” above “developer”. However, those people are usually still developers, yet experienced ones. It is important for them to continue coding, which leaves them little time to explore areas outside software development. Therefore, their sight is often limited to the needs and demands of developers. While they tend to go to great lengths to optimize quality goals related to development time, they often neglect all other stakeholder groups and their needs.

This is not surprising because they never find the time to leave their developer realm and explore the domains of other stakeholders, let alone understand their needs, demands, and pain points. However, their limited point of view keeps them from identifying the best possible solutions (not regarding developers only but all stakeholder groups). It also keeps them from having the discussions needed with other stakeholder groups to make the best decisions possible, as they never understood the other stakeholder groups and were never able to build the empathy needed for such discussions.

The second category is people who never (or only rarely) wrote code. Often, they come from different domains but are good at structured thinking, problem solving and communication – all needed to be a good architect. Often, they are really good at understanding the stakeholder groups outside of IT. However, they are usually also bad at understanding developers and their needs and demands. They are often convinced they do not require a close understanding of developer work to do architectural work.

While it is true that developer work and architectural work are distinct activities, they are still connected in several ways. First of all, without understanding the needs, demands, and pain points of developers, we omit a vital stakeholder group. It also reduces the likelihood that we will come up with a solution that will minimize the overall costs of the solution over its lifetime with a high likelihood. We cannot understand the cost of change without understanding developer needs.

Last but not least, developers are the people who implement the architecture. If they are not convinced of the architecture, they will not implement it. To convince them, you need to get close to them and show empathy. In this respect, developers are not different from any other stakeholder group. Thus, better do not neglect developers. They are stakeholders, too – and they are important stakeholders.

Finally, both types of architects tend to neglect the operations department as they are neither developers nor non-IT stakeholders. However, if we care about systems that run reliably in production, we better also care about them.

Hence, no matter what kind of architect you are, better make sure you address all relevant stakeholder groups.

If you are more of a “developer architect”, this means less coding and more learning to understand people from other domains. But this is what it means to be an architect. It does not mean that you stop coding altogether. But an architect is not a lead developer. These are two different roles for a good reason.

If you are more of a “non-developer architect”, this means learning to understand IT people, developers as well as operations people. You should also try to understand the technology a bit and maybe even do a bit of coding. You will not write production code. But the ability to read code (which requires that you did a bit of coding yourself) and pair with developers can be extremely helpful in discussions with developers.

Moving on

Even if we have discovered the second essential activity, we still have not solved our problem of the missing Why alignment. We can still only tell all the other stakeholder groups about the solution we designed. But we cannot explain to them why it is a sensible solution and only hope they will like it and not question it.

Therefore, I told my discussion peers that Execute is also essential, but that this is still not sufficient and asked them for more. Then, the silence usually lasted a bit longer. Eventually, someone raised their hand and said something like: “Architects always talk about ’trade-offs’. Thus, I think this has something to do with it.” The person just mentioned Evaluate.

Interlude

Let us take a quick break here before moving on to the third “E” of the 4E framework. Otherwise, this post would become quite long again, and I wanted to avoid these very long posts for a change (even if I am not always successful).

In this post, we discussed the two “laws of architectural work” and introduced the idea of the 4E framework. We discussed two of the “E” and named the third one.

In the next post (link will follow), we will discuss the remaining two “E” and complete the framework. Stay tuned …

  1. The fact that architectural decisions are never simply “right” or “wrong” but come with a bundle of pros and cons is often hard to accept for software developers who move into architectural work. Writing code often is about “right” or “wrong”, tests passing or turning red. I.e., you either got your code right or wrong. Architecture is not like that. It is rather about “better” or “worse”. Speaking figuratively: While coding is about 0 or 1, architectural work is about all the numbers between 0 and 1. This is one of the reasons why not every developer makes a good architect, and vice versa. ↩︎

  2. Admittedly, it took me a bit of time to figure out 4 words that all start with “E” that make enough sense to justify a “4E” framework … :) ↩︎

  3. I do not discuss in this post why I recommend making the design of an architecture an explicit activity, as this would distract too much from the original topic of the post. Additionally, it is nothing that could be discussed in a sentence or two. Instead, it has several facets, including exploring the “gray areas”, i.e., where it makes sense to combine architectural design and coding. If you are really curious about this discussion, please ping me, and I may write a blog post discussing this topic. ↩︎

sentences.zh: 支持您组织和指导思想和工作的框架，而不是试图捕获每个可能的细节并强迫您根据您的环境“定制”它们。

blocks.html_en: The 4E framework is no difference. I designed it with Simon Brown’s C4 model in mind: something simple, yet useful, that you can memorize without effort. In its core, it is 4 words 2. As with the C4 model, you may argue that it misses a detail here or there, and it is true. The intention of the 4E framework is not to capture every possible detail. Its intention is to capture the essence of architectural work, and I think it does the job well.

sentences.en: The 4E framework is no difference.
sentences.zh: 4E框架没有区别。

sentences.en: I designed it with Simon Brown’s C4 model in mind: something simple, yet useful, that you can memorize without effort.
sentences.zh: 我设计它时考虑了 Simon Brown 的 C4 模型：简单但有用，您可以轻松记住。

sentences.en: In its core, it is 4 words 2.
sentences.zh: 它的核心是4个词2。

sentences.en: As with the C4 model, you may argue that it misses a detail here or there, and it is true.
sentences.zh: 与 C4 模型一样，您可能会说它在这里或那里遗漏了一些细节，这是事实。

sentences.en: The intention of the 4E framework is not to capture every possible detail.
sentences.zh: 4E 框架的目的并不是捕获每一个可能的细节。

sentences.en: Its intention is to capture the essence of architectural work, and I think it does the job well.
sentences.zh: 它的目的是捕捉建筑作品的本质，我认为它做得很好。

blocks.html_en: Let me explain the 4 parts of the framework in anecdotal form (as it simplifies the memorization even further).

sentences.en: Let me explain the 4 parts of the framework in anecdotal form (as it simplifies the memorization even further).
sentences.zh: 让我以轶事形式解释框架的 4 个部分（因为它进一步简化了记忆）。

blocks.html_en: I discussed architectural work with many people, often, but not always, being developers. When I asked them what the core activities of architectural work are, quick as a shot they came up with Explore.

sentences.en: I discussed architectural work with many people, often, but not always, being developers.
sentences.zh: 我与很多人讨论了架构工作，这些人通常（但并非总是）是开发人员。

sentences.en: When I asked them what the core activities of architectural work are, quick as a shot they came up with Explore.
sentences.zh: 当我问他们建筑工作的核心活动是什么时，他们很快就想到了“探索”。

blocks.html_en: Explore - Find solution options

sentences.en: Explore - Find solution options
sentences.zh: 探索 - 寻找解决方案选项

blocks.html_en: Explore is about designing solution options: designing structures and behavior, combining frameworks, tools, technologies, and more – everything needed to design an architecture. Note that most people talked about designing the solution, i.e., they used the singular form and not the plural form as I did. I will explain in the next post (link will follow) why this distinction is important.

sentences.en: Explore is about designing solution options: designing structures and behavior, combining frameworks, tools, technologies, and more – everything needed to design an architecture.
sentences.zh: 探索是关于设计解决方案选项：设计结构和行为，结合框架、工具、技术等等——设计架构所需的一切。

sentences.en: Note that most people talked about designing the solution, i.e., they used the singular form and not the plural form as I did.
sentences.zh: 请注意，大多数人谈论的是设计解决方案，即他们使用单数形式，而不是像我一样使用复数形式。

sentences.en: I will explain in the next post (link will follow) why this distinction is important.
sentences.zh: 我将在下一篇文章（链接如下）中解释为什么这种区别很重要。

blocks.html_en: The design of an architecture is an essential activity. It also cannot be omitted, as every solution has an architecture, i.e., we always design an architecture. We can only decide if we design the architecture explicitly or implicitly, i.e., accidentally as a byproduct of writing code. While I know there were some proponents of implicit design of an architecture at the peak of the Agile hype, calling it “emergent architecture”, I strongly recommend the explicit variant. 3

sentences.en: The design of an architecture is an essential activity.
sentences.zh: 架构设计是一项重要的活动。

sentences.en: It also cannot be omitted, as every solution has an architecture, i.e., we always design an architecture.
sentences.zh: 它也不能被省略，因为每个解决方案都有一个架构，即我们总是设计一个架构。

sentences.en: We can only decide if we design the architecture explicitly or implicitly, i.e., accidentally as a byproduct of writing code.
sentences.zh: 我们只能决定是显式还是隐式地设计架构，即意外地作为编写代码的副产品。

sentences.en: While I know there were some proponents of implicit design of an architecture at the peak of the Agile hype, calling it “emergent architecture”, I strongly recommend the explicit variant.
sentences.zh: 虽然我知道在敏捷炒作的顶峰时期有一些架构隐式设计的支持者，称之为“新兴架构”，但我强烈推荐显式变体。

blocks.html_en: Oftentimes, architectural work is reduced to the Explore activities. The problem with only designing a solution is that you don’t know if and how the solution delivers to the Why of architecture, as we discussed it in the previous posts. Maybe it creates a working solution. At least we hope so. But does it minimize the cumulative costs of a system over its lifetime without compromising the correctness of behavior at runtime? Does it condense and structure the problem domain and provide guidance and orientation in the solution domain? Does it improve the lives of the people affected?

sentences.en: Oftentimes, architectural work is reduced to the Explore activities.
sentences.zh: 通常，架构工作被简化为探索活动。

sentences.en: The problem with only designing a solution is that you don’t know if and how the solution delivers to the Why of architecture, as we discussed it in the previous posts.
sentences.zh: 仅设计解决方案的问题在于，您不知道该解决方案是否以及如何实现架构的目的，正如我们在之前的文章中讨论的那样。

sentences.en: Maybe it creates a working solution.
sentences.zh: 也许它会创建一个可行的解决方案。

sentences.en: At least we hope so.
sentences.zh: 至少我们希望如此。

sentences.en: But does it minimize the cumulative costs of a system over its lifetime without compromising the correctness of behavior at runtime?
sentences.zh: 但是，它是否可以在不影响运行时行为正确性的情况下最大限度地减少系统在其生命周期内的累积成本？

sentences.en: Does it condense and structure the problem domain and provide guidance and orientation in the solution domain?
sentences.zh: 它是否浓缩和构建了问题领域并在解决方案领域提供指导和方向？

sentences.en: Does it improve the lives of the people affected?
sentences.zh: 它是否改善了受影响人们的生活？

blocks.html_en: Maybe. Maybe not. We do not know. We only designed this solution based on our beliefs in a vacuum (which is another reason why architecture often is a subject of heated, yet groundless discussions).

sentences.en: Maybe.
sentences.zh: 或许。

sentences.en: Maybe not.
sentences.zh: 也许不是。

sentences.en: We do not know.
sentences.zh: 我们不知道。

sentences.en: We only designed this solution based on our beliefs in a vacuum (which is another reason why architecture often is a subject of heated, yet groundless discussions).
sentences.zh: 我们只是基于我们对真空的信念而设计了这个解决方案（这也是建筑经常成为激烈但毫无根据的讨论主题的另一个原因）。

blocks.html_en: Therefore, I told my peers that Explore is good and needed, yet not sufficient. I asked them for more. Usually, this made them think for a moment. Then someone mentioned that architects tend to communicate a lot, and thus, this has to be another activity. I.e., they touched Execute.

sentences.en: Therefore, I told my peers that Explore is good and needed, yet not sufficient.
sentences.zh: 因此，我告诉我的同事们，探索是好的，也是必要的，但还不够。

sentences.en: I asked them for more.
sentences.zh: 我向他们询问更多。

sentences.en: Usually, this made them think for a moment.
sentences.zh: 通常，这会让他们思考片刻。

sentences.en: Then someone mentioned that architects tend to communicate a lot, and thus, this has to be another activity.
sentences.zh: 然后有人提到建筑师倾向于进行大量沟通，因此，这必须是另一项活动。

sentences.en: I.e., they touched Execute.
sentences.zh: 即，他们触及了执行。

blocks.html_en: Execute - Help stakeholders make the best possible decisions

sentences.en: Execute - Help stakeholders make the best possible decisions
sentences.zh: 执行 - 帮助利益相关者做出最佳决策

blocks.html_en: Execute is what I call helping the stakeholders involved make the best possible decisions in their contexts. I do not talk about making decisions as an architect but about supporting other people in making decisions because most of the time, we as architects do not make the decisions. The decisions are made by other stakeholders. Even if we think we make the decisions, more often than not it is an illusion.

sentences.en: Execute is what I call helping the stakeholders involved make the best possible decisions in their contexts.
sentences.zh: 我所说的执行是帮助相关利益相关者在其背景下做出最佳决策。

sentences.en: I do not talk about making decisions as an architect but about supporting other people in making decisions because most of the time, we as architects do not make the decisions.
sentences.zh: 我不是谈论作为建筑师做出决策，而是谈论支持其他人做出决策，因为大多数时候，我们作为建筑师并不做出决定。

sentences.en: The decisions are made by other stakeholders.
sentences.zh: 决策由其他利益相关者做出。

sentences.en: Even if we think we make the decisions, more often than not it is an illusion.
sentences.zh: 即使我们认为我们做出了决定，但通常这只是一种幻觉。

blocks.html_en: E.g., many architects think they decide what architecture gets implemented. But in reality, the developers decide which architecture they implement. If they are convinced that the architecture we designed is good, they will implement it. Otherwise, they will use their significant brainpower to avoid implementing it. Even if we try to force them into implementing “our” architecture by adding reviews and other controls to the process, they will find ways around it. Additionally, it is a futile battle. Energy is wasted that could be used in much better ways.

sentences.en: E.g., many architects think they decide what architecture gets implemented.
sentences.zh: 例如，许多架构师认为他们决定实现什么架构。

sentences.en: But in reality, the developers decide which architecture they implement.
sentences.zh: 但实际上，开发人员决定他们实施哪种架构。

sentences.en: If they are convinced that the architecture we designed is good, they will implement it.
sentences.zh: 如果他们确信我们设计的架构很好，他们就会实施它。

sentences.en: Otherwise, they will use their significant brainpower to avoid implementing it.
sentences.zh: 否则，他们将利用自己重要的智力来避免实施它。

sentences.en: Even if we try to force them into implementing “our” architecture by adding reviews and other controls to the process, they will find ways around it.
sentences.zh: 即使我们试图通过在流程中添加审查和其他控制来迫使他们实施“我们的”架构，他们也会找到解决方法。

sentences.en: Additionally, it is a futile battle.
sentences.zh: 此外，这是一场徒劳的战斗。

sentences.en: Energy is wasted that could be used in much better ways.
sentences.zh: 能源被浪费了，而本可以以更好的方式加以利用。

blocks.html_en: Therefore, I prefer to say that as architects, we support other stakeholders in making good decisions. This requires a lot of communication, collaboration, convincing, and so on. The point is that people usually do not make bad decisions because they are ignorant or malevolent. More often than not, they make bad decisions because they lack relevant information. As an architect, we talk to multiple stakeholder groups, which often gives us information that other stakeholder groups are missing. Organizing this information and sharing it, thereby supporting the different stakeholder groups to base their decisions on a more comprehensive basis, leads to better decisions overall.

sentences.en: Therefore, I prefer to say that as architects, we support other stakeholders in making good decisions.
sentences.zh: 因此，我更愿意说，作为建筑师，我们支持其他利益相关者做出正确的决策。

sentences.en: This requires a lot of communication, collaboration, convincing, and so on.
sentences.zh: 这需要大量的沟通、协作、说服等等。

sentences.en: The point is that people usually do not make bad decisions because they are ignorant or malevolent.
sentences.zh: 关键是，人们通常不会因为无知或恶意而做出错误的决定。

sentences.en: More often than not, they make bad decisions because they lack relevant information.
sentences.zh: 他们常常因为缺乏相关信息而做出错误的决定。

sentences.en: As an architect, we talk to multiple stakeholder groups, which often gives us information that other stakeholder groups are missing.
sentences.zh: 作为一名架构师，我们与多个利益相关者群体进行交谈，这通常会为我们提供其他利益相关者群体所缺少的信息。

sentences.en: Organizing this information and sharing it, thereby supporting the different stakeholder groups to base their decisions on a more comprehensive basis, leads to better decisions overall.
sentences.zh: 组织这些信息并共享它，从而支持不同的利益相关者群体在更全面的基础上做出决策，从而整体上做出更好的决策。

blocks.html_en: Therefore, this is another essential activity.

sentences.en: Therefore, this is another essential activity.
sentences.zh: 因此，这是另一项重要活动。

blocks.html_en: Neglecting relevant stakeholder groups

sentences.en: Neglecting relevant stakeholder groups
sentences.zh: 忽视相关利益相关群体

blocks.html_en: A typical project has a dozen or more stakeholder groups. Each of them has very different needs, a very different view on the project, speaks a different language, and so on. Therefore, it is important to learn to understand them as an architect if you really want to support them in making the best decisions possible in their contexts.

sentences.en: A typical project has a dozen or more stakeholder groups.
sentences.zh: 一个典型的项目有十几个或更多的利益相关者群体。

sentences.en: Each of them has very different needs, a very different view on the project, speaks a different language, and so on.
sentences.zh: 他们每个人都有非常不同的需求、对项目的不同看法、说不同的语言等等。

sentences.en: Therefore, it is important to learn to understand them as an architect if you really want to support them in making the best decisions possible in their contexts.
sentences.zh: 因此，如果您真的想支持他们在他们的环境中做出最佳决策，那么作为架构师，学习理解他们非常重要。

blocks.html_en: This is a place where I often experience shortcomings. Most people who call themselves architects fall into one of two categories:

sentences.en: This is a place where I often experience shortcomings.
sentences.zh: 这是我经常遇到缺点的地方。

sentences.en: Most people who call themselves architects fall into one of two categories:
sentences.zh: 大多数自称为建筑师的人都属于以下两类之一：

blocks.html_en: • “Developer architects”

sentences.en: “Developer architects”
sentences.zh: “开发商建筑师”

blocks.html_en: • “Non-developer architects”

sentences.en: “Non-developer architects”
sentences.zh: “非开发商建筑师”

blocks.html_en: The first ones are typically senior developers who started to take on more responsibility and thus started to call themselves “architects”, often reinforced by enterprise career paths that put “architect” above “developer”. However, those people are usually still developers, yet experienced ones. It is important for them to continue coding, which leaves them little time to explore areas outside software development. Therefore, their sight is often limited to the needs and demands of developers. While they tend to go to great lengths to optimize quality goals related to development time, they often neglect all other stakeholder groups and their needs.

sentences.en: The first ones are typically senior developers who started to take on more responsibility and thus started to call themselves “architects”, often reinforced by enterprise career paths that put “architect” above “developer”.
sentences.zh: 第一批通常是高级开发人员，他们开始承担更多责任，因此开始称自己为“架构师”，通常通过将“架构师”置于“开发人员”之上的企业职业道路来强化。

sentences.en: However, those people are usually still developers, yet experienced ones.
sentences.zh: 然而，这些人通常仍然是开发人员，但经验丰富。

sentences.en: It is important for them to continue coding, which leaves them little time to explore areas outside software development.
sentences.zh: 对他们来说，继续编码很重要，这让他们几乎没有时间探索软件开发之外的领域。

sentences.en: Therefore, their sight is often limited to the needs and demands of developers.
sentences.zh: 因此，他们的目光往往局限于开发者的需求和诉求。

sentences.en: While they tend to go to great lengths to optimize quality goals related to development time, they often neglect all other stakeholder groups and their needs.
sentences.zh: 虽然他们倾向于不遗余力地优化与开发时间相关的质量目标，但他们经常忽视所有其他利益相关者群体及其需求。

blocks.html_en: This is not surprising because they never find the time to leave their developer realm and explore the domains of other stakeholders, let alone understand their needs, demands, and pain points. However, their limited point of view keeps them from identifying the best possible solutions (not regarding developers only but all stakeholder groups). It also keeps them from having the discussions needed with other stakeholder groups to make the best decisions possible, as they never understood the other stakeholder groups and were never able to build the empathy needed for such discussions.

sentences.en: This is not surprising because they never find the time to leave their developer realm and explore the domains of other stakeholders, let alone understand their needs, demands, and pain points.
sentences.zh: 这并不奇怪，因为他们从来没有时间离开自己的开发人员领域并探索其他利益相关者的领域，更不用说了解他们的需求、要求和痛点了。

sentences.en: However, their limited point of view keeps them from identifying the best possible solutions (not regarding developers only but all stakeholder groups).
sentences.zh: 然而，他们有限的观点使他们无法确定最佳的解决方案（不仅涉及开发人员，还涉及所有利益相关者群体）。

sentences.en: It also keeps them from having the discussions needed with other stakeholder groups to make the best decisions possible, as they never understood the other stakeholder groups and were never able to build the empathy needed for such discussions.
sentences.zh: 这也使他们无法与其他利益相关者群体进行必要的讨论以做出最佳决策，因为他们从不理解其他利益相关者群体，也永远无法建立此类讨论所需的同理心。

blocks.html_en: The second category is people who never (or only rarely) wrote code. Often, they come from different domains but are good at structured thinking, problem solving and communication – all needed to be a good architect. Often, they are really good at understanding the stakeholder groups outside of IT. However, they are usually also bad at understanding developers and their needs and demands. They are often convinced they do not require a close understanding of developer work to do architectural work.

sentences.en: The second category is people who never (or only rarely) wrote code.
sentences.zh: 第二类是从未（或很少）编写代码的人。

sentences.en: Often, they come from different domains but are good at structured thinking, problem solving and communication – all needed to be a good architect.
sentences.zh: 通常，他们来自不同的领域，但擅长结构化思维、解决问题和沟通——所有这些都是成为一名优秀架构师所必需的。

sentences.en: Often, they are really good at understanding the stakeholder groups outside of IT.
sentences.zh: 通常，他们非常擅长了解 IT 之外的利益相关者群体。

sentences.en: However, they are usually also bad at understanding developers and their needs and demands.
sentences.zh: 然而，他们通常也不善于理解开发人员及其需求和要求。

sentences.en: They are often convinced they do not require a close understanding of developer work to do architectural work.
sentences.zh: 他们常常相信，他们不需要深入了解开发人员的工作即可进行架构工作。

blocks.html_en: While it is true that developer work and architectural work are distinct activities, they are still connected in several ways. First of all, without understanding the needs, demands, and pain points of developers, we omit a vital stakeholder group. It also reduces the likelihood that we will come up with a solution that will minimize the overall costs of the solution over its lifetime with a high likelihood. We cannot understand the cost of change without understanding developer needs.

sentences.en: While it is true that developer work and architectural work are distinct activities, they are still connected in several ways.
sentences.zh: 虽然开发人员工作和架构工作确实是不同的活动，但它们仍然以多种方式相互联系。

sentences.en: First of all, without understanding the needs, demands, and pain points of developers, we omit a vital stakeholder group.
sentences.zh: 首先，在不了解开发者的需求、需求和痛点的情况下，我们忽略了一个至关重要的利益相关群体。

sentences.en: It also reduces the likelihood that we will come up with a solution that will minimize the overall costs of the solution over its lifetime with a high likelihood.
sentences.zh: 它还降低了我们提出一种解决方案的可能性，该解决方案很有可能最大限度地降低解决方案在其生命周期内的总体成本。

sentences.en: We cannot understand the cost of change without understanding developer needs.
sentences.zh: 如果不了解开发人员的需求，我们就无法了解变更的成本。

blocks.html_en: Last but not least, developers are the people who implement the architecture. If they are not convinced of the architecture, they will not implement it. To convince them, you need to get close to them and show empathy. In this respect, developers are not different from any other stakeholder group. Thus, better do not neglect developers. They are stakeholders, too – and they are important stakeholders.

sentences.en: Last but not least, developers are the people who implement the architecture.
sentences.zh: 最后但并非最不重要的一点是，开发人员是实现架构的人。

sentences.en: If they are not convinced of the architecture, they will not implement it.
sentences.zh: 如果他们不相信该架构，他们就不会实施它。

sentences.en: To convince them, you need to get close to them and show empathy.
sentences.zh: 为了说服他们，你需要接近他们并表现出同理心。

sentences.en: In this respect, developers are not different from any other stakeholder group.
sentences.zh: 在这方面，开发商与任何其他利益相关者群体没有什么不同。

sentences.en: Thus, better do not neglect developers.
sentences.zh: 因此，最好不要忽视开发商。

sentences.en: They are stakeholders, too – and they are important stakeholders.
sentences.zh: 他们也是利益相关者——而且是重要的利益相关者。

blocks.html_en: Finally, both types of architects tend to neglect the operations department as they are neither developers nor non-IT stakeholders. However, if we care about systems that run reliably in production, we better also care about them.

sentences.en: Finally, both types of architects tend to neglect the operations department as they are neither developers nor non-IT stakeholders.
sentences.zh: 最后，两种类型的架构师都倾向于忽视运营部门，因为他们既不是开发人员也不是非 IT 利益相关者。

sentences.en: However, if we care about systems that run reliably in production, we better also care about them.
sentences.zh: 然而，如果我们关心在生产中可靠运行的系统，我们最好也关心它们。

blocks.html_en: Hence, no matter what kind of architect you are, better make sure you address all relevant stakeholder groups.

sentences.en: Hence, no matter what kind of architect you are, better make sure you address all relevant stakeholder groups.
sentences.zh: 因此，无论您是哪种架构师，最好确保您能够解决所有相关利益相关者群体的问题。

blocks.html_en: If you are more of a “developer architect”, this means less coding and more learning to understand people from other domains. But this is what it means to be an architect. It does not mean that you stop coding altogether. But an architect is not a lead developer. These are two different roles for a good reason.

sentences.en: If you are more of a “developer architect”, this means less coding and more learning to understand people from other domains.
sentences.zh: 如果你更像是一名“开发架构师”，这意味着更少的编码和更多的学习来理解来自其他领域的人。

sentences.en: But this is what it means to be an architect.
sentences.zh: 但这就是成为一名建筑师的意义。

sentences.en: It does not mean that you stop coding altogether.
sentences.zh: 这并不意味着您完全停止编码。

sentences.en: But an architect is not a lead developer.
sentences.zh: 但架构师并不是首席开发人员。

content_html_zh:
建筑作品的本质 - 第 5 部分

在上一篇文章中，我们通过审视建筑工作的认知和人性方面，结束了对建筑工作的原因和目的的讨论。 我们还简要讨论了人工智能代理无法满足建筑工作的这些特征，除非你一次又一次地解决已解决的问题。

在这篇文章中，我们将继续讨论建筑工作的下一个维度，即“什么”，并讨论构成建筑工作的不同活动。

建筑工作法则

在我们讨论构成建筑工作的活动之前，让我们首先简要回顾一下“建筑工作的两条法则”。 正如引用的博客文章中所述，它们与其说是实际法律，不如说是“来之不易的发现”。 第一定律是：

每个决定都有其代价。 没有任何决定是免费的。

这意味着建筑工作中没有免费的午餐。 每个决定都有一些优点和一些缺点。 建筑工作没有“对”或“错”。 只有或多或少合适的决定1。 因此，无论有些人试图让您相信什么（通常是购买他们的产品或服务），请放心，他们的“完美”架构并不完美。 他们只是决定隐藏他们所做决定的缺点。

询问如何确定优点和缺点，我们就得出了第二定律：

只能根据决策的背景来评估决策。

架构决策的兴衰是由做出决策的环境决定的。 虽然一个决定在某个地方可能是完全正确的，但在另一个地方可能是无意义的。 简而言之：背景很重要——正如往常一样。

4E框架

有了这两个“法则”，让我们继续进行定义建筑工作的活动。 我开发了一个小框架来组织它们。 请放心：我不会解压 TOGAF 权重框架。 虽然此类框架在某些情况下也可能有其价值，但我并不是它们的忠实粉丝。 我更喜欢最小框架而不是最大框架。 支持您组织和指导思想和工作的框架，而不是试图捕获每个可能的细节并强迫您根据您的环境“定制”它们。

4E框架没有区别。 我设计它时考虑了 Simon Brown 的 C4 模型：简单但有用，您可以轻松记住。 它的核心是4个词2。 与 C4 模型一样，您可能会说它在这里或那里遗漏了一些细节，这是事实。 4E 框架的目的并不是捕获每一个可能的细节。 它的目的是捕捉建筑作品的本质，我认为它做得很好。

让我以轶事形式解释框架的 4 个部分（因为它进一步简化了记忆）。

我与很多人讨论了架构工作，这些人通常（但并非总是）是开发人员。 当我问他们建筑工作的核心活动是什么时，他们很快就想到了“探索”。

探索 - 寻找解决方案选项

探索是关于设计解决方案选项：设计结构和行为，结合框架、工具、技术等等——设计架构所需的一切。 请注意，大多数人谈论的是设计解决方案，即他们使用单数形式，而不是像我一样使用复数形式。 我将在下一篇文章（链接如下）中解释为什么这种区别很重要。

架构设计是一项重要的活动。 它也不能被省略，因为每个解决方案都有一个架构，即我们总是设计一个架构。 我们只能决定是显式还是隐式地设计架构，即意外地作为编写代码的副产品。 虽然我知道在敏捷炒作的顶峰时期有一些架构隐式设计的支持者，称之为“新兴架构”，但我强烈推荐显式变体。 3

通常，架构工作被简化为探索活动。 仅设计解决方案的问题在于，您不知道该解决方案是否以及如何实现架构的目的，正如我们在之前的文章中讨论的那样。 也许它会创建一个可行的解决方案。 至少我们希望如此。 但是，它是否可以在不影响运行时行为正确性的情况下最大限度地减少系统在其生命周期内的累积成本？ 它是否浓缩和构建了问题领域并在解决方案领域提供指导和方向？ 它是否改善了受影响人们的生活？

或许。 也许不是。 我们不知道。 我们只是基于我们对真空的信念而设计了这个解决方案（这也是建筑经常成为激烈但毫无根据的讨论主题的另一个原因）。

因此，我告诉我的同事们，探索是好的，也是必要的，但还不够。 我向他们询问更多。 通常，这会让他们思考片刻。 然后有人提到建筑师倾向于进行大量沟通，因此，这必须是另一项活动。 即，他们触及了执行。

执行 - 帮助利益相关者做出最佳决策

我所说的执行是帮助相关利益相关者在其背景下做出最佳决策。 我不是谈论作为建筑师做出决策，而是谈论支持其他人做出决策，因为大多数时候，我们作为建筑师并不做出决定。 决策由其他利益相关者做出。 即使我们认为我们做出了决定，但通常这只是一种幻觉。

例如，许多架构师认为他们决定实现什么架构。 但实际上，开发人员决定他们实施哪种架构。 如果他们确信我们设计的架构很好，他们就会实施它。 否则，他们将利用自己重要的智力来避免实施它。 即使我们试图通过在流程中添加审查和其他控制来迫使他们实施“我们的”架构，他们也会找到解决方法。 此外，这是一场徒劳的战斗。 能源被浪费了，而本可以以更好的方式加以利用。

因此，我更愿意说，作为建筑师，我们支持其他利益相关者做出正确的决策。 这需要大量的沟通、协作、说服等等。 关键是，人们通常不会因为无知或恶意而做出错误的决定。 他们常常因为缺乏相关信息而做出错误的决定。 作为一名架构师，我们与多个利益相关者群体进行交谈，这通常会为我们提供其他利益相关者群体所缺少的信息。 组织这些信息并共享它，从而支持不同的利益相关者群体在更全面的基础上做出决策，从而整体上做出更好的决策。

因此，这是另一项重要活动。

忽视相关利益相关群体

一个典型的项目有十几个或更多的利益相关者群体。 他们每个人都有非常不同的需求、对项目的不同看法、说不同的语言等等。 因此，如果您真的想支持他们在他们的环境中做出最佳决策，那么作为架构师，学习理解他们非常重要。

这是我经常遇到缺点的地方。 大多数自称为建筑师的人都属于以下两类之一：

  • “开发商建筑师”
  • “非开发商建筑师”

第一批通常是高级开发人员，他们开始承担更多责任，因此开始称自己为“架构师”，通常通过将“架构师”置于“开发人员”之上的企业职业道路来强化。 然而，这些人通常仍然是开发人员，但经验丰富。 对他们来说，继续编码很重要，这让他们几乎没有时间探索软件开发之外的领域。 因此，他们的目光往往局限于开发者的需求和诉求。 虽然他们倾向于不遗余力地优化与开发时间相关的质量目标，但他们经常忽视所有其他利益相关者群体及其需求。

这并不奇怪，因为他们从来没有时间离开自己的开发人员领域并探索其他利益相关者的领域，更不用说了解他们的需求、要求和痛点了。 然而，他们有限的观点使他们无法确定最佳的解决方案（不仅涉及开发人员，还涉及所有利益相关者群体）。 这也使他们无法与其他利益相关者群体进行必要的讨论以做出最佳决策，因为他们从不理解其他利益相关者群体，也永远无法建立此类讨论所需的同理心。

第二类是从未（或很少）编写代码的人。 通常，他们来自不同的领域，但擅长结构化思维、解决问题和沟通——所有这些都是成为一名优秀架构师所必需的。 通常，他们非常擅长了解 IT 之外的利益相关者群体。 然而，他们通常也不善于理解开发人员及其需求和要求。 他们常常相信，他们不需要深入了解开发人员的工作即可进行架构工作。

虽然开发人员工作和架构工作确实是不同的活动，但它们仍然以多种方式相互联系。 首先，在不了解开发者的需求、需求和痛点的情况下，我们忽略了一个至关重要的利益相关群体。 它还降低了我们提出一种解决方案的可能性，该解决方案很有可能最大限度地降低解决方案在其生命周期内的总体成本。 如果不了解开发人员的需求，我们就无法了解变更的成本。

最后但并非最不重要的一点是，开发人员是实现架构的人。 如果他们不相信该架构，他们就不会实施它。 为了说服他们，你需要接近他们并表现出同理心。 在这方面，开发商与任何其他利益相关者群体没有什么不同。 因此，最好不要忽视开发商。 他们也是利益相关者——而且是重要的利益相关者。

最后，两种类型的架构师都倾向于忽视运营部门，因为他们既不是开发人员也不是非 IT 利益相关者。 然而，如果我们关心在生产中可靠运行的系统，我们最好也关心它们。

因此，无论您是哪种架构师，最好确保您能够解决所有相关利益相关者群体的问题。

如果你更像是一名“开发架构师”，这意味着更少的编码和更多的学习来理解来自其他领域的人。 但这就是成为一名建筑师的意义。 这并不意味着您完全停止编码。 但架构师并不是首席开发人员。 这是两个不同的角色，这是有充分理由的。

如果您更多的是“非开发架构师”，这意味着要学习了解 IT 人员、开发人员以及运维人员。 您还应该尝试稍微了解一下该技术，甚至可能编写一些代码。 您不会编写生产代码。 但是，阅读代码（这需要您自己编写一些代码）以及与开发人员结对的能力对于与开发人员的讨论非常有帮助。

继续前进

即使我们发现了第二个基本活动，我们仍然没有解决缺失“为什么”对齐的问题。 我们仍然只能告诉所有其他利益相关者群体我们设计的解决方案。 但我们无法向他们解释为什么这是一个明智的解决方案，只希望他们会喜欢它而不是质疑它。

因此，我告诉我的讨论伙伴，执行也很重要，但这还不够，并要求他们提供更多。 然后，沉默通常会持续更长的时间。 最终，有人举手说道：“建筑师总是谈论‘权衡’。 因此，我认为这与此有一定关系。” 刚才那个人提到了Evaluate。
